transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—thank you for coming in today. What has been bothering you lately or what made you decide to come in now?

I’ve been really worried because I’m convinced some people are watching me and trying to harm me, even though no one else seems to see it. It’s been getting worse over the past month and I’m starting to feel unsafe doing normal things.
Before this past month when things got worse, had you ever experienced similar beliefs or experiences of people watching or trying to harm you, and if so, how long have they been happening in total?

Yeah, I’ve had similar feelings before, like people were watching me or out to get me, but they weren’t as intense as they are now. Thinking back, it’s been going on in some form for a little over two years, maybe around two years and four months.

Aside from feeling watched and targeted, have you noticed hearing voices others can’t hear, your thoughts feeling jumbled or hard to organize, or a big change in motivation or emotional expression over this time?

Yeah, I do hear voices that other people don’t—mostly like a couple of people talking about me or warning me, a few times a day, and that’s been happening on and off for a while. My thoughts and speech feel more jumbled lately, like I lose track of what I’m saying, and I’ve also had way less motivation or interest in things and feel kind of flat emotionally.

Over these past two years, have you had noticeable trouble keeping up with work, school, or daily responsibilities—like losing a job, dropping out, or needing a lot more help at home—because of these experiences, or have you mostly been able to function at your usual level despite them?

I’ve definitely had more trouble keeping up. I ended up leaving my job about a year ago because I was missing shifts and couldn’t focus, and since then I’ve been mostly at home, struggling with basic things like keeping the place clean and staying on top of bills unless my family reminds me.

Have you been using any substances like cannabis, alcohol, stimulants, or other drugs regularly in the past few years, and if so, did your symptoms start or worsen around the times you were using them more?

I drink alcohol sometimes on weekends, but not a lot, and I don’t use cannabis, stimulants, or other drugs regularly. I didn’t notice any clear connection between drinking and when these beliefs or the voices started or got worse.

F20.0 remains the leading candidate. However, given the report of a clear worsening in the past month, I am adding an acute psychotic episode–type condition as a secondary consideration (F23.3) to reflect the possibility that the current presentation might be conceptualized as an acute exacerbation superimposed on a psychotic disorder. Further questioning is needed to clarify the exact time course, presence of any mood episodes, and rule out organic causes, so the list is expanded to [F20.0, F23.3] and is_final remains false.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has had persistent persecutory delusions, auditory hallucinations, negative symptoms (reduced motivation and emotional flattening), disorganized thought/speech, and marked functional decline for over two years, without a clear substance-related cause. This chronic course with characteristic positive and negative symptoms and social/occupational dysfunction is most consistent with paranoid schizophrenia (F20.0). Acute and transient psychotic disorder (F23.3) is less likely because the psychotic symptoms have been present in some form for more than two years, exceeding the brief duration required for F23.x diagnoses.
